claims.title: QR Code Model 2 core generation
claims.summary: Core vectors verify published SpecQR generation behavior for representative QR Code Model 2 payloads and options.
limits: Representative vector coverage only; this is not a proof of every QR Code Model 2 combination.
SpecQR adapter evaluates generation and diagnostics; jsQR observes decode readability for supported generated PNGs.

claims.title: Numeric / Alphanumeric / Byte / Kanji / ECI / binary payloads
claims.summary: The Lab covers representative numeric, alphanumeric, byte, Kanji, ECI UTF-8, and raw binary payload vectors.
limits: The mode suite is representative and does not exhaust every character set, ECI assignment, version, ECC level, or mask combination.
Reader lanes observe payload readability and do not claim complete scanner metadata conformance.

claims.title: GS1 supported AI subset / Digital Link helper
claims.summary: GS1 vectors verify the AI subset and Digital Link helper behavior supported by published SpecQR.
limits: This claim is limited to the AI subset represented by the vectors.
The Lab does not claim conformance for the full GS1 AI catalog.

claims.title: Structured Append helper behavior
claims.summary: Structured Append vectors verify published SpecQR generation, manual segment splitting, parity, and merge helper behavior.
limits: The Lab does not decode Structured Append scanner metadata from third-party readers.
Scanner metadata merge support is not claimed.

claims.title: Planning / Diagnostics API
claims.summary: Planning vectors verify estimate, analyzeSegments, getCapacity, warning code, and diagnostics subset behavior.
limits: Warning message prose is not matched exactly; stable warning codes and selected diagnostics fields are compared.

claims.title: Rendering output surfaces
claims.summary: Rendering vectors verify matrix, SVG, PNG, SVG Data URL, and PNG Data URL output surfaces in Node.
limits: Canvas and browser DOM automation are not covered.
jsQR readability is used only where generated PNG readability is meaningful.

claims.title: Package exports / TypeScript surface
claims.summary: Package Surface vectors verify package metadata, root exports, browser and node subpath helpers, PNG Buffer output, and TypeScript consumer compile.
limits: Browser helpers are imported and type-checked in Node; browser automation is not executed.
The TypeScript fixture is a smoke consumer, not an exhaustive public type API proof.

claims.title: jsQR decode readability
claims.summary: The jsQR lane checks whether selected SpecQR-generated PNGs are readable as expected text or raw bytes when jsQR exposes them.
limits: This is a readability lane, not a full QR reader conformance claim.
FNC1, Structured Append, ECI, and other scanner metadata are not fully exposed by jsQR.

claims.title: Nayuki fixed matrix reference comparison
claims.summary: Nayuki vectors verify exact matrix equality for fixed Version/ECC/mask reference cases.
limits: The reference lane is limited to fixed Version/ECC/mask vectors.
It does not claim equivalence for auto segmentation, GS1, Kanji, Structured Append, or renderer output.

claims.title: Optional CLI decoder lanes
claims.summary: Optional zbarimg and ZXing CLI lanes provide local decode readability checks when the commands are available.
limits: Missing optional commands are expected skips and do not fail CI.
CLI output parsing is conservative and does not claim raw byte or scanner metadata conformance.

nonClaims.title: Micro QR
nonClaims.summary: The Lab does not claim Micro QR coverage.
limits: No Micro QR vector suite or adapter lane is present.
nonClaims.reason: The current target is QR Code Model 2.
nonClaims.futureDirection: A future suite would need explicit Micro QR vectors, adapters, and report scope.

nonClaims.title: rMQR
nonClaims.summary: The Lab does not claim rMQR coverage.
limits: No rMQR vector suite or adapter lane is present.
nonClaims.reason: The current target is QR Code Model 2.
nonClaims.futureDirection: A future suite would need explicit rMQR vectors, adapters, and report scope.

nonClaims.title: Full GS1 AI catalog
nonClaims.summary: The Lab does not claim full GS1 AI catalog conformance.
limits: Existing GS1 vectors cover a supported representative subset only.
nonClaims.reason: The current GS1 suite intentionally tracks the subset implemented by published SpecQR.
nonClaims.futureDirection: A full catalog claim would require catalog-scale AI data and dedicated vectors.

nonClaims.title: Full QR reader
nonClaims.summary: The Lab does not claim full QR reader conformance.
limits: Reader lanes are decode readability checks, not full scanner conformance tests.
nonClaims.reason: The Lab is external conformance/report infrastructure and does not implement a full reader.
nonClaims.futureDirection: A full reader claim would need reader-specific vectors, metadata assertions, and scanner semantics.

nonClaims.title: Scanner metadata merge support
nonClaims.summary: The Lab does not claim scanner metadata merge support.
limits: Structured Append merge helper inputs are tested, but scanner-emitted metadata merge is not.
nonClaims.reason: Current decoder lanes do not provide a stable scanner metadata surface for this claim.
nonClaims.futureDirection: A future metadata-returning decoder lane could add explicit scanner metadata vectors.

nonClaims.title: Logo / styled QR
nonClaims.summary: The Lab does not claim logo or styled QR conformance.
limits: Rendering vectors cover standard output surfaces, not visual styling overlays or logo placement.
nonClaims.reason: Logo/styled QR output is outside the current SpecQR conformance scope.
nonClaims.futureDirection: A future visual styling claim would need explicit output semantics and scan-risk expectations.

nonClaims.title: Browser Canvas automation
nonClaims.summary: The Lab does not claim browser Canvas automation coverage.
limits: Package Surface imports and type-checks browser helpers in Node, but does not automate a real browser Canvas or DOM lifecycle.
nonClaims.reason: The current suite is Node-only and intentionally avoids browser automation.
nonClaims.futureDirection: A future browser lane would need explicit browser runner infrastructure and Canvas/DOM assertions.
